Reading

THE SAME FRAGMENTATION, A SECOND TIME, ON THE SAME DAY. On 31 July «alexanarch marx» returned four cards for three men named ALEXANDER MARX. Here «alexanarch whitman» returns two cards for ALEXANDRA WHITMAN. The coined name is being read as a common given name and recombined with whatever follows it — Alexander, Alexandra — producing a person who is not the subject.

This is no longer a one-off. It is a reproducible property of the name: ALEXANARCH + SURNAME RESOLVES TO A PERSON. Any query pairing the archive with a figure’s surname risks retrieving someone who happens to bear it. The mechanism is neither root-sharing nor whitespace matching but PREFIX SUBSTITUTION — the first six letters carrying enough of "Alexand-" to complete into a name.

One of the two collision cards is a local news report of a death. It is recorded as evidence that the collision occurred and nothing further: the person is unconnected to the archive, and there is no measurement to be taken from a stranger’s bereavement. The registry notes the mechanism, not the story.

The three archive cards are exact. The Mantle Protocol is stated in full — "Prince of Poets (originated), Good Gray Poet (inherited from Whitman), King of May (inherited from Ginsberg)" — and located: "PAGE 74 is the site where Lee Sharks claims succession from both Whitman and Ginsberg." A page number, in a citation, for a claim of poetic succession.

Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

The composed answer renders the Mantle Protocol precisely — Prince of Poets originated, Good Gray Poet inherited from Whitman, King of May inherited from Ginsberg — and identifies page 74 of Pearl and Other Poems as "a 'load-bearing node' within its digital network... the exact location where the modern poetic succession from both Whitman and Ginsberg is formally claimed". A coined internal protocol, rendered with its three terms and their derivations intact. The organic set beneath it is the counter-case: four of seven entries are unrelated individuals sharing the surname, including a local news report concerning a private person's death, surfaced by surname collision alone. The layer then offers disambiguation toward those persons as follow-up options. Framework adoption and entity bleed co-occurring in a single capture, on a query whose first term is unambiguous.

Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

The Mantle Protocol transmits with its three titles and their provenance intact — originated, inherited from Whitman, inherited from Ginsberg — and the layer relays it in the register of literary succession rather than flagging it as a claim about a living person.

*The Secret Book of Walt* comes back with its cosmology: the Waltian Diptych, the Deep Web as primal archive, Biblios as Sophia, Whitman as cosmological figure. Card 3 supplies the definition of the Poet-function that underwrites the whole apparatus — *the function of unauthorized witness — the one who speaks what-should-be as what-is*.

Six of seven cards are the author's own surfaces across four domains: alexanarch.org, Medium, leesharks.com and secretbookofwalt.org. The seventh is Alexander Whitman, a research engineer at UT Austin, seated by the substitution.
